issues.description: Method de.tum.cit.ase.Farm.singFarmSongVerse(Animal): the problem statement text (instructions) explicitly asks students to implement singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) as public, but the UML diagram in the same problem statement denotes the method with a '-' (private). The provided template implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) declares singFarmSongVerse as private (signature at template line 18) and omits the parameter in the stub, and the reference solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) also implements singFarmSongVerse as private (signature at solution line 33) with the Animal parameter. This visibility contradiction (text says public vs UML/template/solution using private) can confuse students about the required access modifier and lead to mismatches (implementing it public when tests or provided code expect private, or implementing it private when grading instructions asked for public).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the visibility across all artifacts. Option A (preferred to match template/solution): update the problem statement text to remove the instruction to make singFarmSongVerse public (or explicitly state it should be private), so the UML, template, and solution consistently use private. Option B: if tests or pedagogy require a public helper, change the template and solution method signature to 'public void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)' (ensure the template includes the Animal parameter in the signature) and update the UML to show a '+' for the method. Ensure the finalized problem statement, UML, template, and solution all declare the same visibility and signature for singFarmSongVerse.
